title: the row's record page is the next page, and it reaches the step
line: once a FamilySearch results page saved for a fetch step has a row that fits the step's person, the plan gives the row's own record a fetch step, a lead, and the fetch list prints that record page in the search link's place, under the record-page name with the row's ark filled, open until a page carrying the ark is archived; the record page saved and collected reaches the lead and, through the listing that pointed at it, the step, is archived under the step's citation, and closes both: the row reads held and the list is empty for it

steps.say: a 1950 citation on the person on the owner's word: the file cites the census on nobody in his household, so the step names the census as the file's own source record for it does (1,62308::0), with no record id of its own, the name the citation sits on as the search was run

step.rationale: harness: a 1950 citation on the owner's word; fetch the record at United States, Census, 1950

expect.why: before the search is saved, the step's own page is open for him

steps.say: the search saved: the first row is his lead, and the row's own record page takes the search link's place on the list

expect.why: the row fits him, so the run is found; the matcher proposes no row
the step's own page is gone from the list: the search was answered and a row of it points on
the plan was written again when the page was attached: the row's record is a lead on his plan
the row's own record page, under the record-page name with the ark filled and the row's year, open for his lead

steps.say: the record page saved in the browser into the download folder under the name the list printed
collect brings it in by its own identity: it reaches the step through the listing that pointed at it and the lead for the row, archived under the step's citation, and both steps are done

expect.why: the page names no sheet the citations name and its principal is Fred, not Frederick, so neither the census-page route nor the collection fallback reaches him: the listing's row does, and the lead the row made
archived under the step's citation, as any record page a step cites
a record page holds the citation: the step is done
the lead's record is archived: done
two runs: the listing, then the record it pointed at
the son alone is proposed on the record page; the household waits on him
the row reads held on the record page
the list is empty for it

steps.say: his plan run again keeps the step done: the archive holds its citation
